chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and associated metabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 65-year-old white male with a history of essential hypertension diagnosed in 2017, currently treated with lisinopril 10 mg. Blood pressure readings show stage‑2 hypertension (SBP 133 mmHg, DBP 98 mmHg). He has longstanding obesity (BMI ≥30), prediabetes (A1c 6.4%), and chronic anemia of unclear etiology. He reports chronic stress and is a victim of intimate‑partner abuse, both contributing to psychosocial strain. Dental health is poor with loss of teeth and recent oral radiographs. He is employed full‑time and has a high‑school education. The patient has had minimal recent healthcare contact (last outpatient visit 2019‑11‑25) and limited laboratory data, with missing lipid panel, renal function, and anemia work‑up. Overall, his clinical picture reflects a metabolic‑syndrome phenotype with multiple untreated or under‑treated risk factors.
